scheme2_name: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Provides guaranteed old-age pension income for unorganised-sector workers aged 18-40.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Creates formal jobs and provides incentives to first-time employees and employers to formalise workforce (01.08.2025-31.07.2027).

comparisons.scheme1_value: Unorganised-sector workers, poor, under-privileged; aged 18-40 at joining; NOT income-tax payers (from 01.10.2022).
comparisons.scheme2_value: First-time formal employees (gross wages up to Rs. 1,00,000/month) and employers covered under EPF & MP Act, 1952.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Guaranteed pension of Rs. 1,000–5,000/month (chosen slab) from age 60 until death; spouse gets same pension after; nominee gets corpus after both pass; tax benefit under section 80CCD(1).
comparisons.scheme2_value: First-timer: one-time cash incentive up to Rs. 15,000 in two instalments (Rs. 7,500 + remainder; 2nd only after Financial Literacy Course). Re-joinees: eligible per EPFO rules.
Monthly incentive for 2 years (4 years for manufacturing): Rs. 1,000–3,000/month per additional employee above baseline, based on wage slab; paid six-monthly after 6 months' ECR filing.

comparisons.scheme1_value: 18–40 years at joining; contributions until age 60; pension from age 60.
comparisons.scheme2_value: No age limit specified; must join an EPFO establishment during 01.08.2025–31.07.2027.
First-timers: gross wages up to Rs. 1,00,000/month at joining; employers can have higher-wage staff.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Must hold active savings bank/post office account with auto-debit enabled; primarily unorganised-sector informal.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Employee must be first-time EPFO contributor (or re-joiner) joining an EPFO-registered establishment; must be formally employed and covered under EPF & MP Act, 1952.

comparisons.scheme1_value: KYC from bank/post office (Aadhaar-based); Aadhaar/mobile for OTP-based eKYC if online; nominee details.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Establishment: PAN, GSTN, Registration Certificate (for manufacturing status), PAN-linked bank account. Employee: Aadhaar-authenticated UAN, Aadhaar-seeded bank account, Face Authentication on UMANG app, monthly ECR filing.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online via net banking or eNPS portal (enps.nsdl.com), or offline at bank/post office branch.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Establishment: EPFO portal deemed registration + PAN/GSTN/bank details update. Employee: UMANG app to generate UAN and complete Aadhaar Face Authentication. No paper form mentioned.

comparisons.scheme1_value: No deadline; can apply anytime between ages 18–40.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Fixed window: 01.08.2025 to 31.07.2027 for new employees and establishments to join.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Pension starts at age 60; no intermediate payments during contribution phase (unless voluntary exit or death).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Employee 1st installment: within 45 days of 6 months' continuous ECR filing + eligibility. 2nd installment: after Financial Literacy Course completion. Employer: six-monthly lump sum after 6 months' ECR filing.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Auto-debit monthly, quarterly, or half-yearly from savings account until age 60. Must maintain sufficient balance; repeated failures attract overdue interest and charges.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Employer files monthly ECRs with EPFO contributions; employee benefits triggered after 6 continuous months' ECR. Employer benefits stop if additional-employment threshold not met that month.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Voluntary exit before 60: refund of own contributions + net accrued income (minus charges); govt co-contribution (pre-31.03.2016) not refunded. Death before 60: spouse can continue or take entire corpus.
comparisons.scheme1_value_note: No early exit mentioned for PM-VBRY; scheme runs fixed term (2 or 4 years for employers); employee benefits stop if ineligible.
comparisons.scheme2_value: No early exit or refund mechanism described; benefits are time-limited (2–4 years) and conditional on ongoing employment and threshold maintenance.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Income-tax payers (from 01.10.2022); if found later, account can be closed.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Employees who joined before 01.08.2025; establishments with pending EPF inquiries (Section 7A/7B/7C), filed FIRs for fraud, or pending/decided Atmanirbhar Bharat Rozgar Yojana irregularities.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Auto-debit must succeed; repeated failures = overdue interest. Income-tax status checked; barred participants risk account closure.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Employee 2nd installment ONLY after Financial Literacy Course (mandatory). Employer benefits stop if additional-employment target missed any month. Seasonal-industry first-timers must stay 6 months. UAN must be Face-Authenticated on UMANG.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Free redressal at npscra.nsdl.co.in (NPS-Lite / CGMS); track via token number. Toll-free: 1800-110-069.
comparisons.scheme2_value: EPFO online redressal system; resolution target 15 days.

recommendation: **Choose APY if:** You are an informal/unorganised-sector worker aged 18–40, NOT a taxpayer, and want guaranteed long-term retirement security with a fixed monthly pension from age 60. It is a **savings-focused, lifetime benefit** scheme. **Choose PM-VBRY if:** You are a **first-time formal employee** (or employer) and want **short-term cash incentives** to formalise employment during 01.08.2025–31.07.2027. It is a **time-limited, employment-incentive** scheme, not a pension. **Key Difference:** APY is **long-term retirement security** (contribute 20+ years, pension for life); PM-VBRY is **near-term employment support** (incentives for 2–4 years, no retirement guarantee). **These schemes serve different needs and are NOT mutually exclusive**—someone could theoretically enrol in both if eligible, but eligibility criteria differ significantly (e.g., income-tax payer status, employment formality). **Disclaimer:** This is AI-assisted guidance based on official scheme documents. For final decisions, verify directly with official portals or contact toll-free helplines. This is not legal or financial advice.
